# Results

## Role dependence of player value measures

Role explained a large share of between-player variance in the box-score indices but almost none in RAPM (@tbl-eta, @fig-bias): η² was `{python} f2(V["eta2"]["PIR40"])` (95% CI `{python} ci(V["eta2_GA95"]["PIR40"])`) for PIR40 and `{python} f2(V["eta2"]["VAL40"])` (`{python} ci(V["eta2_GA95"]["VAL40"])`) for VAL40, compared with `{python} f"{V['eta2']['RAPM']:.3f}"` (`{python} f"{V['eta2_GA95']['RAPM'][0]:.3f} to {V['eta2_GA95']['RAPM'][1]:.3f}"`) for RAPM. Rim protectors and interior bigs had the highest PIR40 and wing/forwards the lowest, whereas RAPM differed little between roles.

The role dependence of PIR was not explained by the overlap between role variables and PIR components, by measurement error or by shrinkage. Among players with the same RAPM, role still explained a substantial share of the variance in PIR40 (partial η² = `{python} f2(CV["kismi_eta2"])`, 95% CI `{python} ci(CV["GA95"])`). At equal RAPM, rim protectors were rated `{python} f"{CV['rol_farki_RAPM_sabit'][rid['Rim protector']]:.1f}"` (95% CI `{python} ci(CV['rol_farki_GA95'][rid['Rim protector']])`) and interior bigs `{python} f"{CV['rol_farki_RAPM_sabit'][rid['Interior big']]:.1f}"` (`{python} ci(CV['rol_farki_GA95'][rid['Interior big']])`) PIR points per 40 minutes higher than `{python} REF`s, and wing/forwards `{python} f"{CV['rol_farki_RAPM_sabit'][rid['Wing/forward']]:.1f}"` (`{python} ci(CV['rol_farki_GA95'][rid['Wing/forward']])`). When RAPM from even-numbered games was instrumented by RAPM from odd-numbered games to correct for its measurement error, these differences were almost unchanged (rim protectors `{python} f"{IV['rol_farki'][rid['Rim protector']]:.1f}"`, 95% CI `{python} ci(IV['rol_farki_GA95'][rid['Rim protector']])`; interior bigs `{python} f"{IV['rol_farki'][rid['Interior big']]:.1f}"`, `{python} ci(IV['rol_farki_GA95'][rid['Interior big']])`; n = `{python} IV["oyuncu_N"]`). With roles derived without PIR components, η² for PIR40 was `{python} f2(V["pir_bilesensiz_roller"]["eta2"]["PIR40"])`, and `{python} f2(V["pir_bilesensiz_roller_kati"]["eta2"]["PIR40"])` when usage, fast-break and second-chance rates were also excluded (RAPM: `{python} f"{V['pir_bilesensiz_roller_kati']['eta2']['RAPM']:.3f}"`). Split-half reliability was `{python} f2(V["guvenirlik"]["PIR40"]["spearman_brown"])` for PIR40 and `{python} f2(V["guvenirlik"]["RAPM"]["spearman_brown"])` for RAPM (n = `{python} V["guvenirlik"]["oyuncu_N"]` players), and reliability-corrected η² was `{python} f"{V['eta2_duzeltilmis']['RAPM']:.3f}"` for RAPM, compared with `{python} f2(V["eta2_duzeltilmis"]["PIR40"])` for PIR40. A weaker RAPM penalty increased the spread of RAPM values (SD `{python} V["rapm_sd"]["ana"]` to `{python} V["rapm_sd"]["l1000"]` points per 100 possessions) without increasing η² (`{python} f"{V['eta2']['RAPM_l1000']:.3f}"`). PIR40 and RAPM were only weakly correlated (*r* = `{python} f2(V["korelasyon"]["RAPM"]["PIR40"])`).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-eta
#| tbl-cap: "Box-score indices differ between roles far more than RAPM does (mean value by main role and share of variance explained by role; players meeting the career-minute threshold)."
m = V["rol_ortalamasi_ham"]
rows = [{"Role": ROLE[k], "Players": V["rol_N"][k], "PIR40": f"{m[k]['PIR40']:.2f}", "VAL40": f"{m[k]['VAL40']:.2f}", "RAPM": f"{m[k]['RAPM']:.2f}"} for k in sorted(m, key=int)]
rows.append({"Role": "η² (95% CI)", "Players": V["oyuncu_N"],
             "PIR40": f"{V['eta2']['PIR40']:.2f} ({ci(V['eta2_GA95']['PIR40'])})",
             "VAL40": f"{V['eta2']['VAL40']:.2f} ({ci(V['eta2_GA95']['VAL40'])})",
             "RAPM": f"{V['eta2']['RAPM']:.3f} ({V['eta2_GA95']['RAPM'][0]:.3f} to {V['eta2_GA95']['RAPM'][1]:.3f})"})
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

![Box-score indices, unlike RAPM, differ systematically between player roles. Bars show the mean of each value measure by main role, standardised across players (z-score), for players meeting the career-minute threshold; error bars are not shown because η² and its confidence interval are given in @tbl-eta.](figures/fig1_role_bias.png){#fig-bias width=90%}

## Out-of-time predictive validity

In 2023–2024 segments, RAPM explained `{python} pp(T["RAPM"])`% of the possession-weighted variance in net rating, compared with `{python} pp(T["PIR40_toplami"])`% for summed PIR40 and `{python} pp(T["VAL40_toplami"])`% for summed VAL40. The advantage of RAPM was `{python} cipp(T["fark_GA95"]["RAPM-PIR40"])` percentage points over PIR40 and `{python} cipp(T["fark_GA95"]["RAPM-VAL40"])` percentage points over VAL40 (95% CIs from game bootstrap), so it was unlikely to be due to chance. Absolute values were small for all predictors, as expected for single lineup segments.

## Within-season validity of lineup value

Per standard deviation of within-team lineup value, second-half net rating changed by `{python} slope("RAPM")` points per 100 possessions for RAPM and `{python} slope("DAKIKA")` for first-half minutes, whereas the confidence intervals of all box-score measures included zero, whether computed from the first half (PIR40 `{python} slope("PIR40_sezon")`) or from all prior data (PIR40 `{python} slope("PIR40_havuz")`; VAL40 `{python} slope("VAL40_havuz")`) (@fig-slope). Box-score values could not be computed for low-minute players and covered `{python} f"{100 * I['kapsam']['PIR40_havuz']:.0f}"`% of segments with pooled data. In the common subset in which all measures were defined (`{python} f"{100 * I['ortak_alt_kume']['segment_payi']:.0f}"`% of segments), the RAPM slope was smaller (`{python} f"{I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM']['egim']:.2f}"`, 95% CI `{python} ci(I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM']['GA95'])`), the minutes slope no longer excluded zero (`{python} f"{I['ortak_alt_kume']['DAKIKA']['egim']:.2f}"`, `{python} ci(I['ortak_alt_kume']['DAKIKA']['GA95'])`), and the paired differences between RAPM and pooled PIR40 (`{python} ci(I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM-PIR40_havuz']['GA95'])`) and minutes (`{python} ci(I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM-DAKIKA']['GA95'])`) included zero. The within-season comparison therefore does not establish that any measure is better than another.

![Within seasons, RAPM-based lineup value and first-half minutes, but none of the box-score indices, have confidence intervals excluding zero. Points: change in second-half net rating per standard deviation of within-team lineup value, adjusted for opponent RAPM and home advantage; bars: 95% team-season bootstrap confidence intervals. Differences between measures were not tested in this figure; see text.](figures/fig2_slopes.png){#fig-slope width=85%}

## Optimised lineups versus the coach's rotation

Second-half segments featuring at least four of the five players given most first-half minutes outperformed the team's other segments by `{python} contrast("DAKIKA_yok")` points per 100 possessions. Optimised fives shared on average about three of five players with this benchmark and were observed in a smaller share of possessions (@tbl-ilp). In direct comparisons within the team-seasons in which both fives were observed, no optimisation variant differed from the coach benchmark under the same constraint: differences ranged from `{python} f"{min(v['fark'] for v in DC.values()):.2f}"` to `{python} f"{max(v['fark'] for v in DC.values()):.2f}"` points per 100 possessions, and all 95% confidence intervals included zero (@fig-ilp). These intervals were wide (up to `{python} f"{max(v['GA95'][1] - v['GA95'][0] for v in DC.values()):.1f}"` points), so differences of several points per 100 possessions in either direction cannot be excluded. Between `{python} f"{100 * min(v['iki_gruba_da_giren_pay'] for v in DC.values()):.0f}"`% and `{python} f"{100 * max(v['iki_gruba_da_giren_pay'] for v in DC.values()):.0f}"`% of the segments featuring an optimised five also featured the coach five and were excluded from these comparisons.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ilp
#| tbl-cap: "Optimised fives share about three players with the coach's most-used five, and direct comparisons show no difference from it (second-half net rating relative to the team's other lineups; direct within-team difference from the coach benchmark under the same constraint; possession share; team-seasons; overlap with the coach five)."
SEL = {"DAKIKA": "Most-used players (coach)", "PIR40_sezon": "PIR40", "VAL40_sezon": "VAL40", "RAPM": "RAPM"}
RULE = {"yok": "none", "tez": "≥ 1 rim protector", "dengeli": "balanced"}
rows = []
for m_ in SEL:
    for r_ in RULE:
        k = f"{m_}_{r_}"
        rows.append({"Selection": SEL[m_], "Constraint": RULE[r_],
                     "vs team's other lineups": f"{C[k]['fark']:.2f} ({ci(C[k]['GA95'])})",
                     "vs coach five (direct)": "—" if m_ == "DAKIKA" else f"{DC[k]['fark']:.2f} ({ci(DC[k]['GA95'])}; {DC[k]['takim_sezon']} team-seasons)",
                     "Possession share": f"{100 * C[k]['hucum_payi']:.1f}%", "Team-seasons": C[k]["takim_sezon"],
                     "Shared with coach five": "—" if m_ == "DAKIKA" else f"{OV[k]:.1f}"})
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

![No optimisation variant differs detectably from the coach's most-used players. Points: direct within-team difference in opponent-adjusted second-half net rating between segments featuring the optimised five (but not the coach five) and segments featuring the coach five (but not the optimised five) under the same constraint; bars: 95% team-season bootstrap confidence intervals.](figures/fig3_ilp.png){#fig-ilp width=85%}
